claim_one_line: THE INTERIOR EXTENSIONS, run as sealed (1d359734; sL-10 item 10 (a)): at the hyperbolic point, B1515's frame carries one generation in one W on the two silver squares. On m135 = -LLRR, at both non-simple kappa = 1 members u = (0, 1/2) and (1/2, 0) (case (a), nu^2 = 1, h^1 = 2 with one interior class), W1 = [[nu (x) rho, c_int], [0, 1]] reads (I(W1), I(Lambda^2 W1)) = (-1, -1): N(10') = N(5bar') = 1 in B1509's dictionary, the SU(5)' anomaly cancelled; routes E (exact over Q(zeta_24)) and N (60 digits) agree class by class; the mechanism as sealed (Lemma A: x cup c_int = 0; Lemma B: the restricted lift mu of c_int lies outside Lambda_A; Jordan type (2, 2), so I(W1) = 0 at every boundary-type class and the four read give (0, -1)); W2, the dual order, reads (+1, +1). Population B at kappa = -1 is not empty (P6 fails): routes T and G read h^1 = 1 at exactly two of 47,333 characters, m136 = +LLRR at the same fibre characters, and both members are case (a) and read (-1, -1) in routes N and W, exactly (route E) and on SnapPy's presentation and holonomy (route S). One interior class on the two states' common double cover (the bundle of (L^2R^2)^2) accounts for both, read exactly. Part C: Lambda_A meet pi_A = 0 at all 31,489 characters chi = nu^2, by rank and by pairing, so no simple member is generation-shaped (Lemma 8). Seven of nine sealed predictions held; G, the golden form of the owner's hypothesis, fails: the members are on the silver squares, and the golden squares and the fourteen golden word states carry none in this census (off m004's levels, by Part C's one cohomology route). Caveats as sealed: the cusp is not sealed (main's interior index, continuous spectrum, B1392); the index does not choose W1 over its dual (Lemma M; main's B1466 at m004's counted point); a non-split W1 is not held by the bare flat action (R76). Not three: one generation per member, and the abelian covers' counts are a finite set of exact readings, sealed separately (a draft bound of two, one-sided, withdrawn). 0 of 19 stays 0.
